title: CS336 overview
text: CS336 is a practical course about building language models from the ground up. The main workflow is tokenizer training, transformer implementation, training loops, scaling decisions, data filtering, and alignment experiments.

title: Tokenizer
text: A tokenizer converts raw text into token ids. A BPE tokenizer starts with byte-level symbols, repeatedly merges frequent pairs, and produces a vocabulary that balances compression and generality.

title: Transformer basics
text: A transformer language model predicts the next token using embeddings, attention blocks, feed-forward layers, layer normalization, and a final projection back to vocabulary logits.

title: Training loop
text: A training loop repeatedly samples batches, runs the model forward, computes cross entropy loss, backpropagates gradients, applies optimizer updates, and logs metrics like loss and tokens per second.

title: Tiny test first
text: Before running expensive training, always run a tiny test. A tiny test checks that the data path, config, model code, optimizer, checkpoint path, and metric logging work together.

title: Scaling rule
text: Scaling should happen only after the small run succeeds. Increase compute by improving GPU target, batch size, context length, model size, or dataset size one step at a time.

title: Data quality
text: Good training data should be readable, relevant, deduplicated, and free of obvious private information. Bad data can make a model memorize noise or produce unsafe answers.

title: OpenTrainer goal
text: OpenTrainer Studio is designed for people who want to create an AI, add their own files, choose a training computer, run a small test, and then scale training when the setup is ready.

title: AI profile
text: An AI profile stores the model name, purpose, data path, training computer, base model, training config, and current status. Each AI should have its own training workspace.

title: External GPU
text: An external GPU target is a remote machine running the same training server. The user saves its URL and optional SSH login, then assigns an AI profile to that machine for training.

title: What should I do after creating an AI?
text: After creating an AI, open its training space, add training materials, choose the training computer, run the tiny test, review the metrics, and only then move to a bigger run.

title: What does loss mean?
text: Loss is a training signal. Lower loss usually means the model is predicting the next token better on the current data, but final quality still needs evaluation with real prompts.
